chunks: I asked him about the man who says, 'On the day I marry so-and-so woman, she is divorced.' So he said: 'It is nothing. Indeed, divorce cannot occur until he has contracted the marriage.'

key_terms.طَالِقٌ: A woman who has been given the pronouncement of divorce (talaq); one who is released from the marriage bond.
key_terms.عُقْدَةَ النِّكَاحِ: The knot/bond of marriage; the contractual tie established by the marriage contract (ʿaqd al-nikah). Controlling or 'possessing' this bond is required before divorce can be issued.
key_terms.يَمْلِكَ: To possess, own, or have authority over something; in legal contexts, to have validly contracted something so as to have rights and obligations regarding it.

ai.seo_question: Is it valid to divorce a woman before marrying her in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Sama'a ibn Mihran narrates asking Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about a man who preemptively declares his future wife divorced before the marriage is contracted. The Imam rules clearly that such a declaration is legally void, establishing the foundational Shia jurisprudential principle that divorce can only be effective when the marriage bond (ʿuqdat al-nikah) already exists. This ruling reflects the broader legal maxim that a legal act cannot take effect on a matter not yet in one's possession or authority.
